subject: Seed indexing sprint handoff + vector DB selection
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Seed indexing sprint handoff + vector DB selection

Hi Jane / Acme team,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week — excited to get the embeddings + rerank onboarding moving. Attached is a concise plan (seed_index_spec_v1.xlsx) and the initial rerank eval prompt set (rerank_eval_prompts.md). High level proposal: 

Phase A — Seed backfill (2 weeks)
- Objective: index ~200k high-priority documents to unblock search QA and rerank evals
- Acceptance: embeddings coverage >= 95% for priority doc types; smoke tests pass on 3 sample queries

Phase B — Full backfill + cutover (3–4 weeks)
- Objective: complete full dataset backfill, enable rerank in low-traffic pilot, collect metrics

Vector DB options we recommend evaluating: managed vector store (hosted), self-hosted FAISS with NVMe nodes, or customer-managed vector DB (if Acme has a preference). Key decision factors: cold-start throughput for backfill, metadata filtering (tags + ACLs), snapshot/restore for audits, and cost per query at current QPS.

Can you confirm the scope for Phase A (which doc types to include) and whether procurement requires an SOW before we start the work? Proposed kickoff: Tue Feb 2, 10:00 PT (we can move if needed).

Action requested from Acme: confirm Phase A doc types and any vendor constraints for third-party DBs (e.g., cannot use managed cloud vendors).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
(attachment: seed_index_spec_v1.xlsx)
(attachment: rerank_eval_prompts.md)

From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: integrations@acme.com
Date: 2026-01-28T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Seed indexing sprint handoff + vector DB selection

Ben — thanks for the clear plan and attachments. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Retention / compliance: we need to ensure the vector DB supports snapshot exports and a 90-day audit trail for vectors/metadata.
2) Procurement: our legal team will likely want an SOW before any vendor spend; we can run the SOW in parallel if you can provide a stub.
3) Preferred DB: we lean toward a managed cloud vector store (less ops), but we need a cost estimate for the two-week seed backfill and for ongoing query traffic at ~200 qps.

Also: can you include any SOC2 / data handling notes in the next version of the spec? If you can get those pieces to us, we can confirm Phase A doc types by EOD Mon Jan 31.

Regards,
Jane Doe
Head of Search, Acme Search
jane.doe@acme.com
(Procurement copy: integrations@acme.com)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-01-29T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Seed indexing sprint handoff + vector DB selection — DB and eval tasks

On Jan 28, Jane asked about compliance and vendor preferences. Quick internal note / proposed assignments: 

- Karthik: run a rapid matrix (3 slides) comparing managed cloud vs FAISS self-hosted vs Redwood-managed dedicated pool. Include: estimated backfill throughput (docs/hr), snapshot/export support, metadata filtering latency, and cost ballpark for seed backfill + steady-state at 200 qps. Deliverable: matrix by Mon Feb 1 COB.

- Monica (me): own rerank evaluation harness setup and initial metrics. I’ll onboard the rerank_prompt set, run 150 sample queries against both baseline and candidate reranker, and produce an MRR/Precision@5 summary for the Feb 2 kickoff. Deliverable: preliminary eval report and a short README for Acme.

- Ben: confirm kickoff time with Acme and share SOW stub + SOC2 pointer. Also coordinate procurement gating.

Notes on an ops approach I prefer: use managed vector store for Phase A to avoid spinning infra; run a short-lived dedicated backfill worker pool (spot + autoscale) with incremental checkpoints so we can resume. For metadata filters, ensure we index tag fields as strings on the vector store side to avoid heavy post-filtering.

I'll start the eval harness tomorrow and ping infra for any quota requests.

—Monica
Product Success Engineer, Redwood Inference
